name: Texo (FormulaNet, 20M), 384x384 equation OCR
summary: Texo, the ~20M-parameter formula-recognition model LatexGen uses as its first-pass equation OCR: an HGNetv2 CNN encoder over a 384x384 grayscale image and a 2-layer mBART decoder that emits LaTeX tokens greedily. Two WebNN graphs: the encoder, which also computes the decoder's cross-attention K/V once per image, and a decode graph that runs k greedy steps per dispatch over static self-attention caches. float16 throughout. A preprocessed image goes in, a token sequence comes out.

source.model: Texo / FormulaNet as shipped in LatexGen public/models/texo (fp32 ONNX export: encoder_model.onnx 54.2 MB, decoder_model_merged.onnx 25.9 MB); upstream Hugging Face id not recorded

decoder.model: mbart (2 layers, d_model 384, 16 heads x 24, ffn 1536, vocab 687, max positions 1027, scale_embedding)

source.precision: float16 throughout, no float32 ops; the fp16 encoder output sits at 1.08x the fp16-on-MPS noise floor and greedy tokens are identical to fp32 on all 18 benchmark images

encoder.role: HGNetv2 encoder + the decoder's cross-attention K/V projections (enc_to_dec_proj folded into k_proj/v_proj), per layer, per head

image.source: LatexGen's texoPreprocess: grayscale, auto-invert to light background, crop to content, resize with the shorter side to 384 onto a black 384x384 canvas, then (x/255 - 0.7931) / 0.1738, rounded to float16
image.note: One channel. The ONNX model takes three identical channels; the graph sums them into stem1's filter. Preprocessing is canvas work and stays in the consumer: the verification inputs are what Chrome's canvas produced, byte for byte.

enc_kT0.role: cross-attention K^T for decoder layer 0, per head; feeds the decode graph on device
enc_kT0.note: readable only because readTensor() on it is the cheapest completion fence

decoder.role: k greedy decode steps in one graph: embedding, 2 mBART layers over static self-attention caches and the encoder K/V, final LayerNorm, lm head, argMax; each step's token feeds the next in-graph

tok.source: the token to feed at the first unrolled step: 0 (<s>) at the start of an image, then the last token of the previous dispatch

step.source: its position: 0, then the number of tokens generated so far

cache_kT0.source: self-attention K cache of layer 0, TRANSPOSED; zeros at the start of an image, then the previous dispatch's cache_kT0_out
cache_kT0.note: an MLTensor cannot be both an input and an output of one dispatch: keep two sets and alternate

enc_kT0.source: the encoder graph's enc_kT0, bound as the SAME MLTensor

tokens.role: the argMax token of each of the k unrolled steps, in order; the consumer stops at the first 2 (</s>) and discards the rest

cache_kT0_out.role: cache_kT0 after k steps; bind as the next dispatch's cache_kT0

chaining.contexts: ONE MLContext for both graphs. navigator.ml.createContext({deviceType: 'gpu'}).
pattern: 1. Allocate the encoder's four K/V outputs once and bind them both as encoder outputs and as the decode graph's enc_* inputs; they never cross into JS.
2. Allocate TWO sets of the four cache tensors (A and B). Per image: writeTensor zeros into set A (the one-hot ADD update needs a clean cache; ~0.1 ms).
3. writeTensor(image); dispatch(encoder). No await: dispatch and writeTensor are ordered on one pipe.

4. tok = 0, step = 0. Loop: writeTensor(tok), writeTensor(step); dispatch(decoder, {tok, step, cache_* from set A, enc_*}, {tokens, cache_*_out into set B}); await readTensor(tokens) -> k int32; append tokens up to and including the first 2 (</s>); stop on </s> or when step + k reaches the cache length; else tok = last token, step += k, swap A and B.
5. Decode the ids with the family tokenizer (WordLevel lookup joined with spaces; apply clean_up_tokenization to match LatexGen's strings).

autoregressive.note: runtime/loader.js autoregressive() implements exactly this from these fields; the cache length is the cache tensors' shape, the unroll factor the tokens output's length.

chaining.everyOutputMustBeBound: WebNN requires every declared output to be bound at dispatch. The four cache outputs are the second tensor set, so nothing is wasted.
chaining.whyUnrolled: On Core ML a dispatch is 0.1 ms but every activation tensor crossing the graph boundary costs ~0.4 ms per 384 KiB in and out, unamortised. One step per dispatch is 1.7 ms per token; 16 steps per dispatch is 0.64.

tokenizer.algorithm: WordLevel over WhitespaceSplit, 687 entries, template <s> A </s>, no normalizer; decoding is a table lookup joined with spaces, plus transformers' clean_up_tokenization_spaces to match LatexGen's recorded strings
tokenizer.produces: decoder.tokens is what it DECODES; nothing is encoded at inference
tokenizer.parity: 18/18 reference sequences decode to LatexGen's recorded strings after clean_up_tokenization (verification/tokenizer_cases.json); encode(decode(ids)) == ids on all of them

constants.note: The encoder blob (31.8 MiB) and the decoder blob (10.3 MiB) are the entry's; a variant with a different unroll factor or cache length has identical weights but different table constants, so the blobs are per-entry for now.

verification.case: LatexGen's 18 image-OCR benchmark items (bench/render-images.py: KaTeX in headless Chrome), preprocessed by LatexGen's own texoPreprocess in Chrome 152, as float16 [1,1,384,384] tensors
verification.reference: fp32 ONNX Runtime running the shipped ONNX files incrementally with their KV cache (webnn-workbench bench/webnn/texo/export_texo.py); torch fp32 and a full fp16 chain on MPS reproduce the same tokens
verification.bar: greedy token ids identical to the reference on every image

notes: Corrections to the model as documented: the encoder emits 144 tokens (12x12), not the 4 the ONNX file's stale declared output shape suggests; the merged decoder's cached branch emits empty present.*.encoder.* tensors, so the encoder-side K/V are computed once, which is what the hoist here relies on.
